title: Tableau Pulse: What It Does, What It Costs and Where It Stops
summary: Tableau Pulse comes with every Tableau Cloud edition, but its agent doesn't. Licensing, a worked cost example, limits and when a data agent fits better.
body_markdown:
*Disclosure: This article is published by Upsolve AI. Where our product appears alongside others, the comparison is based on publicly available information as of November 2026.*


Tableau Pulse is a metrics monitor built into Tableau Cloud: it watches KPIs your data team defines, explains what moved using statistics, and pushes the result to[email, Slack and Microsoft Teams](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_about.htm) . It comes with every Tableau Cloud edition. Its conversational layer, Tableau Agent in Pulse, doesn’t, and Tableau says that layer[does not ask the LLM “to perform math calculations or query data”](https://www.tableau.com/blog/tableau-pulse-enhanced-qa) . That one design choice explains both why Pulse answers are repeatable and why it can’t answer questions its metrics don’t cover.


## Key Takeaways


-


**Pulse is already paid for if you’re on Tableau Cloud.** It’s[listed in all four editions](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/cloud) . The cost is the seat, from $15 per Viewer per month, not the feature.


-


**The agent is a separate purchase.** Tableau Agent in Pulse needs Cloud+ or the Tableau+ Bundle, both contact-sales, plus a connected Salesforce org. Standard and Enterprise sites get a[60-day trial that can’t be paused](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/tableau_gai_trial.htm) .


-


**It answers from metrics, not from your tables.** It[can’t answer questions about columns](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_ask_discover_qa.htm) that aren’t used in a metric, and each metric definition sits on one published data source.


-


**It’s a daily instrument.** Day is the finest time grain, and alerts are[checked once every 24 hours](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_alerts.htm) .


-


**Turn it on first.** If your KPIs are stable and your data is in Tableau Cloud, Pulse is often enough. A data agent earns its cost when questions go beyond the metric list, data spans warehouses, or customers are the users.


## What Is Tableau Pulse?


Pulse has three parts, and the terms matter because the docs use them precisely:


-


**Metric definitions.** A Creator or Explorer (can publish) picks a measure, a time dimension and filterable dimensions from a[single published data source](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_data_source_requirements.htm) . Change the definition once and every metric built on it follows.


-


**Metrics.** A metric is a definition plus a filter and time combination, such as revenue for EMEA this quarter. People follow the ones they care about.


-


**The Insights platform.** It[detects drivers, trends, contributors and outliers](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_insights_platform_insight_types.htm) for each metric, and those findings land in digests sent daily, weekly or monthly.


[Teams digests arrived in August 2026, and full metric unfurls in Slack in October](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_intro.htm) .


Pulse isn’t a dashboard replacement. Tableau built it as the successor to two older features: it[replaced Ask Data and the previous Metrics](https://www.tableau.com/blog/tableau-metrics-and-natural-language-query-evolve-tableau-pulse) in the 2024.1 release, and legacy metrics[didn’t carry over](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_set_up.htm) , so teams had to recreate them. For the wider product verdict, see our[Tableau review](https://upsolve.ai/blog/tableau-review) .

The AI settings are[off by default and independent of the Pulse switch](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_set_up.htm) , so turning on Pulse gives you statistics and no generated text.


Watch two naming problems. Tableau Agent in Pulse was called Enhanced Q&A and Discover until June 2026, and[site settings may still show the old name](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/tableau_gai_trial.htm) . And help pages say “Tableau+” where the[pricing page](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/cloud) now separates Cloud+ Edition from the Tableau+ Bundle.


### How Pulse relates to Tableau’s other AI products


Checked against the[edition table](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/cloud) in November 2026:


-


**Tableau Agent** is the assistant across the product: in Pulse, Authoring, Dashboards, Prep and Catalog. All Cloud+ and Bundle only.


-


**Tableau Knowledge** builds governed knowledge graphs from metadata and semantics to give agents context. Cloud+ and Bundle.


-


**Tableau Next** is a separate platform[enabled by Data 360 and the Salesforce platform](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/to_tab_plus_features.htm) . It’s sold in the Bundle. Partner[Keyrus notes it needs data ingested and configured in that environment first](https://keyrus.com/us/en/insights/tableau-next-vs-tableau-pulse-vs-tableau-which-is-right-for-your-organization) .


-


**Tableau MCP** is in every edition, and this is the sleeper. Its[tool list](https://tableau.github.io/tableau-mcp/docs/intro) lets any MCP client read Pulse definitions and generate insight bundles on all SKUs. Only the AI-written insight brief is gated to Tableau+. If you want Pulse statistics inside your own agent, you may not need the upgrade.

There is no Pulse line item. You pay for Tableau Cloud seats, and[every deployment needs at least one Creator](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/cloud) .

Capacity-based Viewer Blocks replace named Viewer seats, are priced by sales and can’t be mixed with role-based Viewers on one deployment. Our[Tableau pricing guide](https://upsolve.ai/blog/tableau-pricing) covers the rest of the price list.


Tableau says Cloud has[no consumption-based component](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/cloud) , with one exception worth reading: pairing select AI features with Audit Trail in Data 360 can consume credits. The Bundle includes 250K credits.


### What Pulse costs when you extend it


The real cost appears when you extend Pulse to people without a seat. Say you want to reach 200 business users on role-based Viewers:


-


Standard: 200 × $15 = **$3,000 a month**


-


Enterprise: 200 × $35 = **$7,000 a month**


Those seats include dashboards, digests and guided Q&A. They don’t include the agent. To price that, you need a quote, because Tableau publishes no Cloud+ number. A useful way to read one: on a 300-user site, each $10 per user per month above Enterprise adds $36,000 a year (300 × $10 × 12).


A data agent prices differently. Upsolve Team, on[annual billing](https://upsolve.ai/pricing) to match Tableau’s terms, is $1,600 a month with 10,000 credits and $0.04 per extra credit. A standard analytical question uses 5-10 credits.


These aren’t equivalent products: a Viewer seat also buys dashboards, and it buys Pulse push rather than open questions. Warehouse compute is extra on both sides.


## How Tableau Pulse Answers a Question, and Where It Stops


Ask Tableau Agent in Pulse why churn rose, and the[Pulse Insight Service](https://www.tableau.com/blog/tableau-pulse-enhanced-qa) does the computing using governed definitions and statistical logic. The model then writes up what came back, with citations to the metrics behind it.


> The trade is simple. Pulse can’t write a bad query because it doesn’t write one, and it can’t answer anything the metric list didn’t anticipate.


It isn’t immunity from error. Tableau’s docs still warn that[hallucinations can occur](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_ask_discover_qa.htm) , especially on complex questions.


### Limits in the data


-


**One data source per definition.**[No workbook-embedded sources and no blending](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_data_source_requirements.htm) unless you combine the data before publishing. Goal values must live in that same source. If your KPI spans Snowflake and Postgres, someone has to model it into one published source first.


-


**Time series only, at day grain or coarser.** Tableau says hour or minute data isn’t a good fit. Pair that with a[24-hour alert check](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_alerts.htm) and weekly default digests, and Pulse isn’t an operational alerting tool.


-


**Simple aggregations.** Sum, average, median, maximum, minimum, count and distinct count, plus an advanced editor. One practitioner,[Kateryna Drogaieva, wrote in August 2026](https://drogaieva.medium.com/tableau-pulse-when-your-business-doesnt-fit-the-metric-2e878048842a) that Pulse failed her school-year business: fiscal labels confused users, period comparisons misled on seasonal data, and retention-style lookup metrics wouldn’t carry through. That’s one team’s experience, and it predates the[October 23 release](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_intro.htm) that lets the agent answer about any date, but test your fiscal calendar and retention metrics first.


### Limits in the agent


-


**It only sees metrics.** No[unused columns or data source metadata](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_ask_discover_qa.htm) . “Is this data certified?” is Tableau’s own example of a question it can’t answer.


-


**Metrics that don’t match get dropped.** Filtering or comparing works only across metrics sharing traits like time granularity and dimensions. Others are left out of the answer, so check the Metric Sources list.


-


**What you follow shapes the answer.** It reads all metrics you follow in a group, and too many can overload the context window. Tableau’s advice is to follow fewer.


-


**Hard numbers.** Top and bottom lists[default to 7 members, 50 at most](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_intro.htm) . Correlations appear only at a coefficient of 0.7 or higher, among[up to five candidates](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_insights_platform_insight_types.htm) an author chose in advance.


### Rollout traps admins find late


-


**The trial clock can’t stop.** Try AI[runs for 60 days even if you turn the agent or Pulse off](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/tableau_gai_trial.htm) , and it also turns on Tableau Agent in Prep. Have metrics ready before you start. Afterward, buying means[connecting a Salesforce org with Einstein generative AI set up](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_set_up.htm) , which the trial skipped.


-


**Turning Pulse off doesn’t stop it.** The[services keep querying data sources and sending digests](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_set_up.htm) after the setting goes off. Former users keep getting digests they can’t open or unfollow, so remove followers first. On live connections, assume those queries still hit your warehouse.


-


**Group limits don’t reach the API.** Restricting Pulse to one group[isn’t enforced at the external API level](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_set_up.htm) , which matters for embedding.


-


**Permissions live on the data source.** You[can’t deny access to an individual metric](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_set_up.htm) , and there’s no setting to limit who creates metrics, since filtering an existing one creates a new one. Row-level security on the source is respected.


-


**Data residency has a footnote.** LLM requests route to the nearest region, but[fall back to US Azure OpenAI if that region is unavailable](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_intro.htm) . The fallback can’t be disabled, and only Tableau+ customers can see it in audit logs.


## When a Dedicated Data Agent Fits Better


Start with the case for staying. If your data is in Tableau Cloud, your KPIs are stable and your users mostly want to know when something moves, use Pulse. A digest nobody has to ask for is a different product from a chat box, and for an executive who lives in Slack it may be the better one. The incremental cost is zero for anyone already holding a seat. If you’re leaving Tableau for other reasons, that’s a[different comparison](https://upsolve.ai/blog/tableau-alternatives) .


A data agent such as[Upsolve](https://upsolve.ai/pricing) fits better when:


-


**Questions go past the metric list.** Upsolve’s agent[retrieves schema, looks up golden examples, generates SQL and runs it](https://docs.upsolve.ai/ai-agent-builder/agent-observability) , so it can reach any table you’ve exposed. The cost is that a model is writing the query, and[Upsolve’s docs say answers can be wrong](https://docs.upsolve.ai/slack/overview) . The control is[golden queries that double as test cases](https://docs.upsolve.ai/ai-agent-builder/golden-assets) (tests are in beta), plus a full trace of each answer. You’re choosing between bounded answers and open ones you have to test.


-


**Data spans warehouses.** Upsolve[works across Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift and Postgres at the same time](https://upsolve.ai/) , without first merging data into one published source. No existing semantic layer is required to start.


-


**Your customers are the users.** Pulse can be[embedded through connected apps](https://help.tableau.com/current/api/embedding_api/en-us/docs/embedding_api_pulse.html) , and serving external users without named seats points you to capacity-based licensing, priced by sales. Upsolve Team includes embedding, multi-tenant support and row-level security[enforced by the platform on every query](https://docs.upsolve.ai/ai-agent-builder/data-governance) . See also[Tableau embedded analytics](https://upsolve.ai/blog/tableau-embedded-analytics) .


-


**People want to ask where they already work.** Pulse pushes digests to Slack and Teams, and Tableau lists the agent on[the Pulse home page, metric pages and mobile](https://www.tableau.com/blog/tableau-pulse-enhanced-qa) .[Upsolve answers in a Slack thread](https://docs.upsolve.ai/slack/overview) , and in Teams, an embedded SDK or an MCP client.


-


**You want context outside one vendor.** Pulse definitions live inside Tableau, reachable from outside through its MCP server. Agent Studio context sits outside any one warehouse or BI tool.


The two can coexist: Pulse for the recurring KPI push, an agent for the follow-up question. For how the rest of the category sorts out, see the[AI BI tools roundup](https://upsolve.ai/blog/ai-business-intelligence-tools) .

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is Tableau Pulse?


Tableau Pulse is a feature of Tableau Cloud that monitors metrics you define and sends personalized insights to[email, Slack and Teams](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_about.htm) . It explains changes using statistical analysis, with optional AI-written summaries.


### What is the difference between Tableau and Tableau Pulse?


Tableau is the full platform for building data sources, workbooks and dashboards. Pulse is a layer on top of it for people who don’t open dashboards: it reads published data sources and pushes metric changes to them. You need Tableau Cloud to use Pulse.


### How much does Tableau Pulse cost?


There’s no separate charge. It’s[included in all Tableau Cloud editions](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/cloud) , which start at $15 per Viewer per month on Standard, with at least one Creator at $75. Tableau Agent in Pulse needs Cloud+ or the Tableau+ Bundle, priced through sales.


### Does Tableau Pulse work on Tableau Server?


No. Tableau’s help says[Pulse is available for Tableau Cloud](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/pulse_about.htm) . Tableau[attributed that to the Einstein Trust Layer](https://www.tableau.com/blog/tableau-metrics-and-natural-language-query-evolve-tableau-pulse) in 2024, and said Server customers would lose Ask Data and Metrics on upgrading to 2024.2.


### Is Tableau worth learning in 2026?


Yes, if your company runs it or you’re aiming at teams that do. Pulse raises the value of that skill rather than removing it, since every metric depends on a well-modeled published data source that somebody has to build.


### What is replacing Tableau?


Nothing, going by Tableau’s own pages. Pulse replaced Ask Data and the old Metrics, not Tableau itself, and Tableau’s[pricing page](https://www.tableau.com/pricing) still sells Cloud, Server and Next side by side. If you’re weighing a switch, see our[Tableau alternatives guide](https://upsolve.ai/blog/tableau-alternatives) .


Write down ten questions your users ask that your Pulse metrics can’t answer. If the list is short, stay with Pulse. If it’s long, you can[check Upsolve’s pricing](https://upsolve.ai/pricing) or[book a demo](https://upsolve.ai/demo) and run those questions against your data.
